facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old man presented with gross hematuria
Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
A staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter without evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

concepts.why: Intravenous urography and retrograde ureteropyelography demonstrated a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter
Intravenous urography and retrograde ureteropyelography demonstrated a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, which could be a polyp
Although urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy were negative for malignancy, the presence of a tubular mass in the mid ureter raises the possibility of ureteral carcinoma
Intravenous urography and retrograde ureteropyelography demonstrated a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, which could be causing a stricture
Gross hematuria and microscopic hematuria are common symptoms of nephrolithiasis
Gross hematuria and microscopic hematuria can be symptoms of pyelonephritis, although the patient's symptoms and test results do not strongly support this diagnosis
Intermittent right pelvic pain and the presence of a tubular mass in the mid ureter could be caused by ureteral inflammation
Intermittent right pelvic pain and the presence of a tubular mass in the mid ureter could be caused by a ureteral injury
The patient's 60-pack-year smoking history increases the risk of various smoking-related illnesses, including ureteral cancer
The patient's history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis increases the risk of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, including tuberculosis of the ureter

rationales.F01: Gross hematuria is a common symptom of ureteral tumors and carcinomas.
rationales.F06: A 60-pack-year smoking history increases the risk of various smoking-related illnesses, including ureteral carcinoma.
rationales.F09: Intravenous urography demonstrating a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter is highly suggestive of a ureteral tumor or carcinoma.
rationales.F10: Retrograde ureteropyelography confirming a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels is highly suggestive of a ureteral tumor or carcinoma.
rationales.F11: Negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy results make ureteral carcinoma less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with gross hematuria, intermittent right pelvic pain, and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, along with negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy for malignancy, supports the diagnosis of a ureteral polyp over a ureteral tumor.
